dedupe_keys.name: iucn global standard for nature based solutions second edition and self assessment tool

description: The IUCN Global Standard for Nature-based Solutions is a framework for designing, verifying and scaling up nature-based solutions so that they address societal challenges while delivering benefits for people and biodiversity. It covers 8 criteria with 27 indicators, from societal challenges, an integrated systems perspective, biodiversity and ecosystem integrity, financial feasibility and inclusive governance to trade-offs, adaptive management and mainstreaming, each with guiding questions, and it is meant for use at local, national and global levels by governments, businesses, funders and communities. It is published by IUCN in Gland, Switzerland; the second edition (2026, doi 10.2305/KKSO4573) revises the first edition of 2020, and an International Standard Committee revises the criteria every four years. The standard is available as a free PDF of 56 pages under CC BY-NC 4.0, and the IUCN Nature-based Solutions portal hosts an online self-assessment tool that is free with no usage limits and produces a report. Caveats: it is a qualitative assessment framework, not a dataset of projects, and non-commercial terms apply to reuse of the document. It supports screening and appraisal of green-blue infrastructure schemes and sets shared terms for climate adaptation projects; a related record is the Oppla nature-based solutions repository.
